chunks: My father (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to me, he said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ahmad, on the authority of Musa ibn Umar, on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hussein ibn Ribat, on the authority of some of his men, that Abi 'Abdullah (peace be upon him) said:
The believing servant continues to be recorded as doing good as long as he remains quiet; but when he speaks, he is recorded as doing good or doing bad.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of silence in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the spiritual discipline of *hims* (restraint) as a continuous source of merit, reflecting the Shia emphasis on guarding the tongue as a prerequisite for righteous action. The hadith illustrates the dynamic nature of divine accounting, where silence serves as a default state of goodness, while speech introduces the potential for both reward and liability based on its content. This concept aligns with the scholarly view that silence is not merely absence of speech but an active form of worship and self-purification.
